title: Fallen-object definition — create/permit-fall presupposed, not inside praedestinatio
source_text: XXXV. Qui vero putant hominem lapsum & peccatorem in praescientia divina esse objectum praedestinationis, & consequenter negant hominis creationem & peccati permissionem inter effectus praedestinationis debere numerari, sic eam definiunt, ut non complectatur decretum divinum de homine creando, & lapsu ejus permittendo, sed decretum istud ab ea praesupponatur, tanquam aliquid prius, secundum nostrum concipiendi modum. Ubicunque vero non convenit de rei definitione, certum est ibi multum esse logomachiae & contentionis verbalis.
pass_a_gloss: But those who think fallen and sinful man in the divine foreknowledge to be the object of predestination, and consequently deny that man’s creation and the permission of sin ought to be numbered among the effects of predestination, so define it that it does not embrace the divine decree of creating man and of permitting his fall, but that that decree is presupposed by it as something prior, according to our way of conceiving. But wherever there is no agreement concerning the definition of the thing, it is certain that there is much logomachy and verbal contention.
pass_b_english: Fallen-object party: object = fallen sinner in divine foreknowledge.
Create-and-permit-fall decrees are presupposed prior — not inside praedestinatio.
Where definition is not shared, verbal contention is certain.
